newsitem.title: INDIA: India authorises 250,000 tonnes sugar exports.
newsitem.headline: India authorises 250,000 tonnes sugar exports.

text.p: The Indian government has authorised the export of 250,000 tonnes of sugar in the 1996/97 (October-September) season, the Commerce Ministry said on Friday.
"It has been decided to release a ceiling of 250,000 tonnes for export of sugar from the free sale quota of 1996/97 sugar season," the ministry said in a statement.

It said the authorisation would include 20,000 tonnes of sugar for export by the Indian Sugar and General Industry Export-Import Corporation (ISGIEC) to the European Union and the United States under an existing preferential arrangement.
The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) would issue the licences for the export of sugar during the season, the statement said.
It was the first export authorisation since the government ended ISIGEC's monopoly over sugar exports in January.
India produced a record 16.4 million tonnes of sugar in 1995/96 and expects an output of about 14 million tonnes in 1996/97.
